From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 2 Mar 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Indemnity — order form redlines (HelixCloud)

Hey Chris,

Following up with the redlines attached to the OF for the 3-pool Dedicated purchase. Legal has flagged a couple of items I wanted to surface so we can try to avoid back-and-forth in procurement:

- Defense vs. reimbursement: our standard is "right to defend" for third-party IP claims on the services we provide; Helix's markup proposes a reverse (customer-defend) for a broad set of outputs. Can you confirm if that was intended to sweep in AI-generated outputs?
- OSS and third-party data carveouts: we can't accept blanket indemnity for claims that flow from OSS dependencies or customer-provided inputs without a carveout.
- Liability cap alignment: our procurement team prefers a multiple of the annual order value rather than an unlimited/very high cap.

Attached: Helix_OrderForm_redline_v2.docx — we've added inline language and a short note on evidence/cooperation timelines.

Would Helix legal be open to a short 30-minute sync this week to walk the redline together? If so, propose Thu 3/3 10:30am PT.

Thanks —
Ben
VP, Sales
Redwood Inference
(415) 555-0147

From: Chris Morgan <chris.morgan@helixcloud.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: contracts@helixcloud.com
Date: Fri, 2 Mar 2028 12:02:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Indemnity — order form redlines (HelixCloud)

Ben — thanks for the redline and the heads-up. I pulled in contracts to confirm our view. Quick summary from Helix: we can accept a "right to defend" for claims alleging that our hosted service, as delivered, infringes a third party's IP; however, we have concerns about language that would require Helix to defend claims arising from customer prompts, customer data, or third-party OSS where the claim stems from those elements.

Two counterpoints we want to raise:
1) Narrowly tailored mutual indemnity: Helix proposes mutual indemnity for third-party claims that the service as configured and operated by the vendor (Redwood) infringes IP, and customer indemnity for claims tied to customer inputs and outputs.
2) AI output carveout ask: we are seeing some vendors attempt to push all risk for model outputs onto customers; for procurement and our internal risk team that is a non-starter — any indemnity that touches generated output needs to be tightly limited to direct infringement (not content quality issues) and should exclude third-party OSS where possible.

I've attached a short note with line-by-line comments: helix_redline_notes.pdf. We can do Thu 3/3 10:30am PT; that works for our counsel. If you want us to propose specific redline text, we can do a follow-up after the call.

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 2 Mar 2028 15:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Indemnity — order form redlines (HelixCloud)

Thanks Ben — I reviewed Chris's notes. High level thoughts and proposed strawman for the call:

1) Defense/resolution allocation
- We keep "right to defend" for Redwood where the claim alleges infringement by the Service as delivered. We offer to reimburse reasonable settlement amounts if we don't defend.

2) Carveouts (non-negotiables)
- Explicit carveout for OSS and third-party dependencies that Redwood did not author.
- Carveout for customer-provided data, prompts, and post-processing/derivative uses where customer controls output dissemination.

3) AI-generated output (practical compromise)
- We are willing to accept indemnity for direct third-party IP claims that can be tied to the Service's internal models/weights (narrow), subject to notice/cooperation and a dollar cap. We push back on open-ended indemnity tied to all "generated content."

4) Caps / insurance offset
- Cap: lesser of (a) 3x annual committed spend under the OF, or (b) $5M.
- Insurance offset/priority: if customer has primary coverage for a particular claim, allow offset but keep a residual indemnity obligation for Redwood where we control the defense.

Suggested meeting objectives for Thu 3/3 10:30am PT:
- Walk Helix's counterpoints live and agree on carveouts.
- Land a redline we can hand back to procurement for approval (avoid going back and forth on text).

Redline text snippet (for discussion):
"Vendor shall defend Customer against any third-party claim that the Vendor's Service, as provided hereunder, infringes a third party's patent, copyright, or trademark, provided that such claim does not arise from Customer Content, customer-supplied prompts, or pre-existing open-source components not authored by Vendor. Vendor's liability under this Section shall be subject to the Cap set forth in the Order Form."

Action items:
- Kimberly: I'll bring the snippet and a short internal memo on evidence/cooperation timelines to the call (attached - redline-snippet.txt).
- Ben: ask Helix to confirm whether their "generated output" language is intended to capture all model outputs or only uses they control.
- Laura: prepare procurement exception request template if Helix insists on a higher-than-typical cap.

Will dial in for Thu.

Kimberly Park
Head of Contracts, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai
